- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 73.0), model often overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates the drop; add 1–2% buffer below true low to avoid under-shock.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after sentiment shift); forecast first 3–5 days should be 1–2% below true outcome to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.5–0.75), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before applying trend adjustment.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 75.44 → 70.88), model often holds too high; apply 10–15% downward correction if sentiment is weak or neutral.
